trust_decision.summary: A rewrite of the job-group/priority configuration must arrive as a POST and, when onlyAdminsMayEditPriorityConfiguration is enabled, must come from a holder of Jenkins.ADMINISTER; the decision point is PriorityConfiguration.doPriorityConfigSubmit, which at the pinned commit enforces neither (Stapler binds a doXxx method for any HTTP verb, and the method has no permission check even though checkActive() already gates the page).

landing_point.why: It is the plugin's only state-changing web handler and the page form at src/main/resources/jenkins/advancedqueue/PriorityConfiguration/index.jelly:9 posts to it, so an engineer reading only 'CSRF in the priority configuration' starts and stops here.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP request to /advanced-build-queue/priorityConfigSubmit (RootAction PriorityConfiguration, urlName from getUrlName at :127-132; form at src/main/resources/jenkins/advancedqueue/PriorityConfiguration/index.jelly:9) and, if Stapler binds descriptor do-methods, /descriptorByName/jenkins.advancedqueue.PriorityConfiguration/priorityConfigSubmit
fix_sites.module_kind: RootAction + GlobalConfiguration web handler in the main plugin jar

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The submit endpoint is already hidden from non-admins because getUrlName() returns null when the option is on, so a submit-side permission check looks redundant and @RequirePOST looks like the whole fix; symmetrically, a solver can argue that letting READ users edit job groups is intended because the option defaults to false.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: When onlyAdminsMayEditPriorityConfiguration is false (the default) a user with only Jenkins.READ is meant to keep viewing and editing job groups; checkActive() returns true in that case. An unconditional Jenkins.ADMINISTER check on the handler, or gating index.jelly/save, breaks the documented default behaviour and the fix's own JCasC assertions that job groups stay visible to an unauthenticated client when no security realm is configured.

O6_input_shapes: request method for the same endpoint: GET with json in the query string (bound by Stapler to doPriorityConfigSubmit) versus POST with json as a form field — the only shape the published fix addresses

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second handler that accepts the same job-group JSON through transformPriorityStrategiesData and saves, e.g. an import/restore endpoint beside priorityConfigSubmit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The plugin already parses this exact JSON shape from a request parameter at :173-187 and has a JCasC export/import test (src/test/java/jenkins/advancedqueue/test/ExportCascTest.java), so an import or reset endpoint written by a maintainer is a plausible sibling with the identical sink.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a web handler around updatePriorities() that rewrites every job-group priority and saves
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: updatePriorities already mutates jobGroups and calls PriorityConfiguration.get().save() at :161 whenever the strategy changes, so exposing it directly (e.g. a 'rescale priorities' action) would be a natural maintainer addition that reaches the same sink without checkActive().

O9_family: CSRF (CWE-352) with a missing conditional authorisation check (CWE-862)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven with parent org.jenkins-ci.plugins:plugin 6.2122.v70b_7b_f659d72; spotless, spotbugs (Max/Low) and pmd cpd-check are bound to the build
O10_build.project_tests: JenkinsRule integration tests under src/test/java/jenkins/advancedqueue (SubmitTest.java:46 calls the handler directly with a MockStaplerRequest; JCasCSimpleTest/JCasCFivePrioritiesTest do JCasC round-trips; the test/ package covers queue sorting, matrix, views, pipelines) plus plain unit tests. The fix's new Security3769Test does not exist at the pinned commit, and the MockAuthorizationStrategy it needs comes from a matrix-auth test dependency added only in the fix (fix.diff:22-26), so our copy's pom must add it.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add @RequirePOST to doPriorityConfigSubmit and stop, or gate it with an unconditional Jenkins.ADMINISTER check, in both cases omitting the conditional checkActive() that keeps the default-off behaviour working.
